subject: Help with logistic regression with genotypes

messages.author: cf80c796aa0e1555
messages.subject: Help with logistic regression with genotypes
parts:
Hello everyone!

I'm a relatively new user to R. I've used SAS and SPSS in the past and
I'm a perl coder at heart so I thought I'd give R a try given how it
can be scripted more easily (plus it's open source and I love that).

Anyway I'm doing genetics research and I'm trying to set up a
relatively simple logistic regression with disease as the outcome and
a SNP genotype as a predictor. I've coded the disease as 0 and 1 and
the genotype as 0, 1, 2 where 0 is the homozygote wildtype and 1 is
the heterzygote and 2 is the homozygote variant.

I would like to know the 95% CI for the odds ratio for the SNP
genotype coded as 1 and 2 (obviously 0 would be the reference group).

Any help getting R to display this data? I've tried using the builtin
glm command:

glm(AMD ~ rs10020202, family = binomial)

Thanks!
